cards.explanation: The answer is writing. The LORD tells Moses, Israel's leader, “…I will write on them the words that were on the first tablets…” (Exodus 34:1). Moses brings the chisel and the LORD brings the words. If it were up to me, friends, those tablets would come back with a typo and a smudge.

The answer is False. The LORD says, “No one may go up with you; in fact, no one may be seen anywhere on the mountain…” (Exodus 34:3). Moses makes this climb alone. No buddy, no cheering section, and nobody to carry the second tablet.

The answer is that no flocks or herds may graze there. Moses climbs up alone, and the LORD says, “…not even the flocks or herds may graze in front of the mountain.” (Exodus 34:3). No one may be seen anywhere on that mountain. Think of the emptiest, quietest spot you've ever stood in, friends, and then take away the sheep too.

The answer is in a cloud. The text says, “And the LORD descended in a cloud, stood with him there…” (Exodus 34:5). He comes down and stands right there with Moses. Moses came up the mountain to be with Him, and now he is.

The answer is that He is slow to anger. The LORD calls Himself “…compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, abounding in loving devotion and faithfulness…” (Exodus 34:6). Slow to anger, and abounding in loving devotion. My patience gets tested when the oven timer beeps for the fifth time, friends, and He's out here abounding.
The answer is True. The LORD says He is “…maintaining loving devotion to a thousand generations…” (Exodus 34:7). A thousand generations. I can't even keep track of one batch on a busy day, friends.

The answer is False. The LORD does not say He will leave the guilty unpunished. He says, “Yet He will by no means leave the guilty unpunished…” (Exodus 34:7). That line comes right after He describes Himself as forgiving.

The answer is go with us and forgive us. Moses says, “…please go with us. Although this is a stiff-necked people, forgive our iniquity and sin…” (Exodus 34:9). He asks for the LORD's company and for forgiveness. Moses doesn't ask for a bunch of extras, friends.

The answer is False. The LORD says, “All the people among whom you live will see the LORD’s work, for it is an awesome thing that I am doing with you.” (Exodus 34:10). So they will notice. Nobody's going to miss it.

The answer is False. The LORD says, “Be careful not to make a treaty with the inhabitants of the land you are entering…” (Exodus 34:12). He doesn't want Israel making treaties with them. He gives the reason in the same verse.
The answer is that they would trap Israel. The LORD says a treaty could make them “…a snare in your midst.” (Exodus 34:12). A snare is a trap. He's warning Israel before they walk into it, friends.

The answer is to tear them all down. The LORD says, “…you must tear down their altars, smash their sacred stones, and chop down their Asherah poles.” (Exodus 34:13). Tear down, smash, chop. That's three different verbs for one clear job.
The answer is god. The LORD says, “…you must not worship any other god…” (Exodus 34:14). That's the reason for tearing everything down. He wants Israel's worship for Himself.

The answer is True. The LORD says that when those people “…prostitute themselves to their gods and sacrifice to them, they will invite you, and you will eat their sacrifices.” (Exodus 34:15). That's what a covenant with them could lead to. It starts as an invitation and ends up somewhere He warned about.

The answer is to make none for yourselves. The LORD says, “You shall make no molten gods for yourselves.” (Exodus 34:17). One sentence, and no fine print. No loophole for a small one to keep on the shelf, friends.

The answer is forty days and forty nights. The text says, “So Moses was there with the LORD forty days and forty nights…” (Exodus 34:28). The text adds that he went without eating bread or drinking water the whole time. I get dizzy if I skip one cookie break, friends.

The answer is False. The text says Moses was there with the LORD “…forty days and forty nights without eating bread or drinking water.” (Exodus 34:28). So he ate no bread and drank no water. That's a long stretch.

The answer is his face. The text says, “…his face had become radiant from speaking with the LORD.” (Exodus 34:29). It was his face, not anything he was carrying or wearing. He came down from that mountain shining.

The answer is False. The text says Moses “…was unaware that his face had become radiant from speaking with the LORD.” (Exodus 34:29). He had no idea. Aaron and all the Israelites looked at him and saw that his face was radiant (Exodus 34:30).

The answer is False. Aaron, Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14), and all the Israelites “…were afraid to approach him.” (Exodus 34:30). Moses doesn't hold back, though. He calls out to them, and then Aaron and the leaders come back to him (Exodus 34:31). Nobody rushes, but they do come.
The answer is that he calls out to them. The text says, “But Moses called out to them…” (Exodus 34:31). He doesn't leave and he doesn't wait around. He calls them over, and they come.

The answer is True. The text says, “And after this all the Israelites came near…” (Exodus 34:32). Earlier they were afraid to approach him (Exodus 34:30), and now they're standing right there. From scared to front row, friends.

The answer is that he passes on the LORD's commands. The text says, “…Moses commanded them to do everything that the LORD had told him on Mount Sinai.” (Exodus 34:32). He brings down what the LORD told him. All of it.

The answer is removes. The text says, “…whenever Moses went in before the LORD to speak with Him, he would remove the veil until he came out.” (Exodus 34:34). So the veil comes off when he goes in. It stays off until he comes out.
